chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mad'ani from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar al-Sabati who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who rinses his mouth (mutamadmad) and water enters his throat while he is fasting. He said, 'There is no penalty upon him if he did not intend it.' I said, 'And if he rinses a second time and water enters his throat?' He said, 'There is no penalty upon him.' I said, 'If he rinses a third time?' He said, 'He has erred, but there is no penalty upon him and no making up (qada) is required.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water entering the throat while rinsing the mouth during fasting?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the gradation of liability in fasting when water enters the throat during rinsing, distinguishing between simple unintentional entry and excessive repetition. While the second instance is excused, the third is deemed 'ihsan' (a minor fault or error in conduct) yet still requires no penalty or qada, reflecting the Shia principle of leniency in matters of doubt (shubha) during worship. This ruling underscores the distinction between intentional consumption (which breaks the fast) and mere entry of water, emphasizing that deliberate intent (ta'ammud) is the key determinant for invalidation.
